newsitem.title: UK: Russian capital outflows to continue - U.S official.
newsitem.headline: Russian capital outflows to continue - U.S official.

text.p: Capital outflows from Russia will continue until investments there become profitable and there is a regulatory regime which investors are comfortable with, a U.S. treasury official said on Monday.

"There is a lot of western funds and capital that is very interested...but it will only end up in investments when those are profitable and there is a regulatory and legal regime in which people can be reasonably assured they are going to be treated fairly," David Lipton, assistant secretary at the U.S. treasury told Reuters Financial Television.

Lipton was speaking after addressing the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), set up in 1991 to assist Soviet bloc countries with the transition to market economies.
He said that unless there was confidence in the system, money would continue to flow out of Russia.

"In the absence of that, and until that is secured...there will be some capital outflows. What we have is an interesting situation where Russians are saving and like foreign investors are not willing to put all of their money into Russian investments," Lipton said.

He said the U.S. was very encouraged by Russian President Boris Yeltsin's recent speech in which he showed renewed commitment to reform and covered important subjects such as improving the tax and legal systems, strengthening property rights and fighting crime and corruption.

Lipton described Yeltsin's recent appointments as "a new economic dream team" and said it would be harder to imagine a stronger team of reformers. "The agenda for reform is well-known...the question is whether Russia, given its political circumstances, will be able to advance the reform agenda."
The U.S. had, he said, had discussions with the Russian government about the improvement of the tax administration.
"We are hopeful that the new economic team will tackle these issues," he added.
